(a) \(\text{CH}_3\text{Cl}\)

subtopic: Tetravalence of Carbon: Shapes of Organic Compounds
stem:
Write the state of hybridisation of carbon in the following compounds and shapes of each of the molecules.
(a) \(\text{H}_2\text{C}=\text{O}\)
(b) \(\text{CH}_3\text{F}\)
(c) \(\text{HC}\equiv\text{N}\)
solution:
(a) \(sp^2\) hybridised carbon, trigonal planar.

(b) \(sp^3\) hybridised carbon, tetrahedral.

(c) \(sp\) hybridised carbon, linear.

stem:
Expand each of the following condensed formulas into their complete structural formulas.
(a) \(\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COCH}_2\text{CH}_3\)
(b) \(\text{CH}_3\text{CH}=\text{CH}(\text{CH}_2)_3\text{CH}_3\)
solution:
(a) The complete structural formula shows every atom and every bond:

\(\text{H}-\overset{\text{H}}{\underset{\text{H}}{\text{C}}}-\overset{\text{H}}{\underset{\text{H}}{\text{C}}}-\overset{\text{O}}{\text{C}}-\overset{\text{H}}{\underset{\text{H}}{\text{C}}}-\overset{\text{H}}{\underset{\text{H}}{\text{C}}}-\text{H}\)

that is, a five-carbon chain \(\text{H}_3\text{C}-\text{CH}_2-\text{C}(=\text{O})-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_3\) in which the third carbon carries a doubly bonded oxygen and each of the other four carbons carries its full complement of C–H bonds.

(b) A seven-carbon chain with a double bond between the second and third carbons:

\(\text{H}-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}=\text{CH}-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_3\)

written out in full as \(\text{H}_3\text{C}-\text{CH}=\text{CH}-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_3\), every C–H bond shown explicitly, the two doubly bonded carbons carrying one hydrogen each.
_note: The book prints both solutions as fully drawn complete structural formulas (every C, H and bond line). They are transcribed here in an equivalent written form.

stem:
For each of the following compounds, write a condensed formula and also their bond-line formula.
(a) \(\text{HOCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)\text{CH}_3\)
(b) The structure in which a central \(\text{CH}\) carries an \(\text{OH}\) group above it and a \(-\text{C}\equiv\text{N}\) group on each side: \(\text{N}\equiv\text{C}-\text{CH}(\text{OH})-\text{C}\equiv\text{N}\)
solution:
Condensed formula:

(a) \(\text{HO}(\text{CH}_2)_3\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)_2\)

(b) \(\text{HOCH}(\text{CN})_2\)

Bond-line formula:

(a) A six-carbon zig-zag chain drawn with \(\text{HO}\) at one end, a methyl branch on the fourth carbon and a second methyl branch on the fifth carbon (an isopropyl terminus).

(b) A single carbon vertex carrying \(\text{OH}\) above it, with \(\text{NC}-\) on one side and \(-\text{CN}\) on the other.

stem:
Expand each of the following bond-line formulas to show all the atoms including carbon and hydrogen.
(a) A cyclohexane ring bearing a branched three-carbon group attached through its middle carbon (an isopropyl substituent).
(b) An unbranched eight-vertex zig-zag chain.
(c) A chain drawn as \(\text{HC}\equiv\text{C}-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}(\text{OH})-\text{CH}_3\) in bond-line form, the \(\text{OH}\) written below the fourth vertex.
(d) Two \(\text{CH}\) vertices joined to each other, each carrying two methyl groups.
solution:
(a) The ring is a six-membered carbon ring; drawing every atom gives a ring of six carbons, four of them \(\text{CH}_2\), one \(\text{CH}\) bearing the side chain, and the side chain itself is \(-\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)\text{CH}_3\); the complete structural formula shows the ring carbons with their hydrogens and the branch carbon carrying one hydrogen and two methyl groups.

(b) \(\text{H}-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{H}\), i.e. an eight-carbon chain in which each of the two end carbons carries three hydrogens and each of the six inner carbons carries two.

(c) \(\text{H}-\text{C}\equiv\text{C}-\overset{\text{H}}{\underset{\text{H}}{\text{C}}}-\overset{\text{H}}{\underset{\text{OH}}{\text{C}}}-\overset{\text{H}}{\underset{\text{H}}{\text{C}}}-\text{H}\)

(d) \(\text{H}_3\text{C}\) and \(\text{CH}_3\) above, \(\text{H}_3\text{C}\) and \(\text{CH}_3\) below, joined to the two central carbons:

\((\text{H}_3\text{C})(\text{H}_3\text{C})\text{CH}-\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)(\text{CH}_3)\), each central carbon also carrying one hydrogen.
_note: The stem in the book is FOUR DRAWN BOND-LINE FORMULAS with no text; they are described in words here. The printed solution (a) is on page index 3 and (b)-(d) continue on page index 4.

stem:
Structures and IUPAC names of some hydrocarbons are given below. Explain why the names given in the parentheses are incorrect.
(a) \(\text{CH}_3-\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)-\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_3\)
2,5,6-Trimethyloctane [and not 3,4,7-Trimethyloctane]
(b) \(\text{CH}_3-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}(\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3)-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_3\)
3-Ethyl-5-methylheptane [and not 5-Ethyl-3-methylheptane]
solution:
(a) Lowest locant number: the set 2,5,6 is lower than 3,5,7 (the book compares the locant sets obtained by numbering from the two ends), so numbering must begin from the end that gives 2,5,6.

(b) The substituents are in equivalent positions; the lower number is given to the one that comes first in the name according to alphabetical order. Ethyl precedes methyl alphabetically, so ethyl gets locant 3.

stem:
Write the IUPAC names of the compounds i–iv from their given structures.
(i) \(\text{CH}_3-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}(\text{OH})-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_3\)
(ii) \(\text{CH}_3-\text{CH}_2-\text{CO}-\text{CH}_2-\text{CO}-\text{CH}_3\)
(iii) \(\text{CH}_3-\text{CO}-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{COOH}\)
(iv) \(\text{CH}\equiv\text{C}-\text{CH}=\text{CH}-\text{CH}=\text{CH}_2\)
solution:
(i) The functional group present is an alcohol (\(-\text{OH}\)); hence the suffix is '-ol'. The longest chain containing \(-\text{OH}\) has eight carbon atoms, so the corresponding saturated hydrocarbon is octane. The \(-\text{OH}\) is on carbon atom 3 and a methyl group is attached at the 6th carbon. Hence the systematic name is **6-Methyloctan-3-ol**.

(ii) The functional group present is a ketone (\(>\text{C}=\text{O}\)), hence suffix '-one'. Presence of two keto groups is indicated by 'di', so the suffix becomes 'dione'. The two keto groups are at carbons 2 and 4. The longest chain contains 6 carbon atoms, hence the parent hydrocarbon is hexane. Thus the systematic name is **Hexane-2,4-dione**.

(iii) Here two functional groups, namely ketone and carboxylic acid, are present. The principal functional group is the carboxylic acid group; hence the parent chain will be suffixed with 'oic' acid. Numbering of the chain starts from the carbon of the \(-\text{COOH}\) functional group. The keto group in the chain at carbon 5 is indicated by 'oxo'. The longest chain including the principal functional group has 6 carbon atoms; hence the parent hydrocarbon is hexane. The compound is therefore named **5-Oxohexanoic acid**.

(iv) The two \(\text{C}=\text{C}\) functional groups are present at carbon atoms 1 and 3, while the \(\text{C}\equiv\text{C}\) functional group is present at carbon 5. These groups are indicated by suffixes 'diene' and 'yne' respectively. The longest chain containing the functional groups has 6 carbon atoms; hence the parent hydrocarbon is hexane. The name of the compound is therefore **Hexa-1,3-dien-5-yne**.
_note: Parts (i) and (ii) with their solutions are on page index 10; the solution to (iii) and the whole of (iv) are on page index 12 (page index 11 is Table 8.4).

stem: Derive the structure of (i) 2-Chlorohexane, (ii) Pent-4-en-2-ol, (iii) 3-Nitrocyclohexene, (iv) Cyclohex-2-en-1-ol, (v) 6-Hydroxyheptanal.
solution:
(i) 'hexane' indicates the presence of 6 carbon atoms in the chain. The functional group chloro is present at carbon 2. Hence the structure of the compound is \(\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}(\text{Cl})\text{CH}_3\).

(ii) 'pent' indicates that the parent hydrocarbon contains 5 carbon atoms in the chain. 'en' and 'ol' correspond to the functional groups \(\text{C}=\text{C}\) and \(-\text{OH}\) at carbon atoms 4 and 2 respectively. Thus the structure is \(\text{CH}_2=\text{CHCH}_2\text{CH}(\text{OH})\text{CH}_3\).

(iii) A six-membered ring containing a carbon–carbon double bond is implied by cyclohexene, which is numbered so that the double bond lies between C-1 and C-2. The prefix 3-nitro means that a nitro group is present on C-3. The double bond is a suffixed functional group whereas \(\text{NO}_2\) is a prefixed functional group, therefore the double bond gets preference over the \(-\text{NO}_2\) group in numbering. The structure is cyclohexene carrying \(-\text{NO}_2\) at C-3.

(iv) '1-ol' means that an \(-\text{OH}\) group is present at C-1. \(\text{OH}\) is a suffixed functional group and gets preference over the \(\text{C}=\text{C}\) bond. Thus the structure is a cyclohexene ring carrying \(-\text{OH}\) at C-1 with the double bond between C-2 and C-3.

(v) 'heptanal' indicates the compound to be an aldehyde containing 7 carbon atoms in the parent chain. The '6-hydroxy' indicates that an \(-\text{OH}\) group is present at carbon 6. Thus the structural formula of the compound is \(\text{CH}_3\text{CH}(\text{OH})\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CHO}\). The carbon atom of the \(-\text{CHO}\) group is included while numbering the carbon chain.

stem:
Write the structural formula of:
(a) o-Ethylanisole
(b) p-Nitroaniline
(c) 2,3-Dibromo-1-phenylpentane
(d) 4-Ethyl-1-fluoro-2-nitrobenzene
solution:
(a) A benzene ring carrying \(-\text{OMe}\) (\(-\text{OCH}_3\)) and, on the adjacent (ortho) carbon, \(-\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\).

(b) A benzene ring carrying \(-\text{NH}_2\) and, on the opposite (para) carbon, \(-\text{NO}_2\).

(c) \(\text{C}_6\text{H}_5-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}(\text{Br})-\text{CH}(\text{Br})-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_3\): a five-carbon chain whose C-1 bears the phenyl group and whose C-2 and C-3 each bear a bromine.

(d) A benzene ring carrying \(-\text{F}\) at C-1, \(-\text{NO}_2\) at C-2 and \(-\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\) at C-4.
_note: The book prints all four answers as drawn ring structures; they are transcribed here in words. Problem 8.10 sits at the top of page index 14, i.e. it belongs to section 8.5.4 (Nomenclature of Substituted Benzene Compounds), not to section 8.6 Isomerism which begins lower on the same page.
